title: Graduated acceptance PRD for multi-lane hosted API with SLA bucketization and canary cutover
creator: Lena Park
description:
Goal: Define a graduated acceptance PRD for hosted API endpoints (generation/chat, embeddings, rerank) that enforces per-lane SLA bucketization, telemetry-driven cutover criteria, and a canary cutover plan with automated rollback triggers. This ticket clarifies scope, acceptance criteria, and a minimal safe launch checklist so engineering and SRE can run a predictable progressive rollout across tenants and regions.

Scope (in):
- Define lanes (fast, standard, cost-optimized) and mapping rules to SLA buckets.
- Acceptance criteria tied to telemetry signals (latency p95, errors, cost per token, eval-based quality regressions).
- Canary cutover plan: segmentation rules, ramp schedule, automated rollback thresholds, migration playbook.
- Pre-launch verification steps and post-launch monitoring targets.

Scope (out):
- Long-term billing UI changes (will be a follow-up).
- Dedicated capacity quota management (separate project).

Stakeholders: PM (Lena), Eng leads (Omar, Priya Shah), SRE (Marcus Li), DX (Nina Gomez), Legal (Aisha Khan).

Assumptions:
- KV cache improvements from ENG-52780 are available in staging.
- Model variants with quantization profiles are already cataloged.
- Tenant tagging metadata is present for customer segmentation.

Success metrics:
- No more than 0.1% customer-facing increased error rate attributable to rollout.
- Latency p95 within SLA band for 95% of tenants after ramp.
- Zero severity-1 incidents tied to canary cutover in first 72 hours.

Notes: This PRD is intentionally conservative: the first launch is minimal—covering three lanes and two regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1).
acceptance_criteria: All lanes (fast/standard/cost-optimized) have documented mapping to SLA buckets and default routing policies.
Pre-launch telemetry dashboard shows baseline metrics for selected tenants and regions for 7 days in staging.
Canary cutover automation deployed in staging and validated with synthetic traffic (ramp and rollback behavior verified in CI).
Automated rollback triggers defined: latency p95 increased >20% vs baseline for >5m, error rate >2% absolute increase for >2m, or quality eval AUC drop >3% on smoke prompts.
Rollout runbook completed and signed off by Eng lead, SRE, and PM (signatures in linked docs).
SDKs and API surface notes updated with explicit lane selection parameters and default behaviors.
Security review completed and any required notes added to launch checklist.
Smoke eval harness produces pass/fail reports for generation and embeddings with defined pass thresholds.
Cost gating: token-cost regression per model <= 10% vs baseline for canary tenants or fallback engaged.
launch_checklist: Create tenant group(s) for canary (10 internal tenants + 5 pilot customers), document consent where required.
Confirm KV cache warmup scripts and population strategy for canary tenants.
Deploy canary automation runbook: ramp 0->5% (30m), 5->25% (2h), 25->100% (24h) with manual holdpoints.
Preflight load test: synthetic traffic at x1.5 expected production QPS for 30m with no SLA violations in staging.
Verify telemetry pipelines (inbound events, schema) are receiving lane tags and tenant ids. Dashboards validated.
Alerting: SLO burn alert at 50% and 80% thresholds, and PagerDuty rotation for canary window.
Docs: Update API reference with lane selection enum, examples, and degradation behavior for fallback models.
SDK: Patch release notes and deprecation notice where behavior diverges from previous defaults.
Legal/Compliance: confirm data residency constraints for pilot tenants in eu-west-1.
Sign-off meeting scheduled with Eng/SRE/PM (date/time + attendee list).
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Staging Validation): run synthetic smoke + evaluation harness; baseline collection (7 days).
Phase 1 (Internal Canary): route 10 internal tenant keys (ops) to new lanes for 72h; automated checks only; manual approval required to proceed.
Phase 2 (Pilot Customers): add 5 pilot customers with written consent; ramp to 25% over 6h; guardrails active; SRE on-call.
Phase 3 (Regional Rollout): after 48h stable pilot, open to region (us-west-2) at 50% over 24h, then eu-west-1 repeat; cross-region fallback available.
Phase 4 (Full Launch): gradual global ramp to 100% over 72h with continuous monitoring and final postmortem 7 days after completion.
telemetry_signals: Latency: p50/p95/p99 per-lane, per-tenant, and aggregated (percentile trend windows 1m/5m/1h).
Availability: 5xx/4xx error rates by endpoint type and tenant.
Quality: eval-harness AUC/accuracy on golden prompt set (generation and embeddings).
Cost: per-token cost delta vs baseline model and quantization profile, batch size distribution.
Cache-hit rates: prefix/KV cache effectiveness per tenant and lane.
Model fallback frequency: count and rate of fallback activations per hour.
